title: Reduce streaming disconnect partial-token regressions by hardening resume heuristics and KV-cache consistency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a regional capacity event on 2026-03-08 we observed an uptick in streaming client disconnects that manifested as partial-token responses and resume failures. Root cause analysis shows a race between async KV-cache eviction (triggered by autoscale & memory compaction) and the resume heuristic that trusts a per-session KV signature. When the cache entry was evicted while a reconnecting client attempted to resume, the runtime returned a short token chunk (partial token) or failed to resume and dropped the connection. This was exacerbated by aggressive prefix flushing in the de-dup layer and insufficient backpressure signaling to the gateway tier.

Reproduction steps (dev environment):
1) Run a simulated load generator that opens long-lived streaming sessions with intermittent network jitter.
2) Force a cache compaction/eviction on the serving node (test harness provided in /contrib/kv-evict-sim).
3) Trigger scale-down of the node group to cause transient cache invalidation timing.
4) Observe partial tokens and resume failures in the stream traces and the resume mismatch logs.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix):
- Add a conservative resume-validation period: when a session reconnects within N seconds (configurable default 15s), fallback to a temporary in-memory write-through buffer that reconstructs the last 64 tokens even if the KV signature is missing.
- Disable aggressive prefix flush in the de-dup layer for sessions flagged as resumable during the hotfix window.
- Short-term admission control: throttle new streaming sessions on oversubscribed nodes to reduce concurrent KV churn.

Planned durable fixes (this ticket):
1) Make KV-cache eviction deterministic with session-affinity-aware compaction windows (design + implementation).
2) Strengthen resume protocol: include last-seen token index and checksum in the resume fragment; if mismatch, fetch from sibling replica before returning partial tokens.
3) Improve backpressure propagation from runtime -> gateway -> client to avoid uncontrolled prefix flushes under load.
4) Add server-side token assembly validation that prevents delivering incomplete token bytes to the network (deliver only whole Unicode scalar boundaries and whole token units as defined by tokenizer).
5) Instrument new SLOs/alerts: resume-failure-rate, partial-token-rate, kv-mismatch-rate; add Grafana dashboards and PagerDuty playbooks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary rollout (runtime-1.21) shows >90% reduction in partial-token events on canary hosts during a simulated compaction + jitter test.
- Resume-failure-rate below 0.01% for canary traffic for 24h under synthetic load.
- New metrics emitting; runbooks created and linked in the ticket.

Longer-term follow-ups (separate tickets):
- Evaluate persistent per-session KV checkpoints for large multi-turn sessions to reduce dependency on in-memory caches.
- Consider protocol-level idempotency markers for streaming token fragments to support at-least-once delivery semantics for clients that can tolerate duplicates.
